answer: The anchor multiplier is published, charged in river, and copper lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 501 identities would post 2092 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
